normalizations_and_actual_objects.obligation: TV is the normalized event distance sup over measurable B of abs(P(B)-Q(B)); for probability densities it equals one half of the L1 difference.
normalizations_and_actual_objects.consequence: For measurable h in [0,1], the expectation gap is at most TV, with no extra factor of two.

normalizations_and_actual_objects.obligation: Full O(n) Haar is probability measure; its determinant +1 and -1 components each have mass 1/2; mu_{n,b} is the conditioned probability measure.
normalizations_and_actual_objects.consequence: H(lambda) is half the difference of the two mixture test expectations, so TV >= 2 abs(H(lambda)). Conditioning must normalize by component mass.

normalizations_and_actual_objects.obligation: A_O = ((kappa+1)/2) I_n - ((kappa-1)/4)(O + O^T), and the Gaussian is centered with covariance A_O^{-1}.
normalizations_and_actual_objects.consequence: P_b is the actual measure-valued average of N(0,A_O^{-1}) over mu_{n,b}, not a mixture of precisions, a Gaussian with averaged covariance, a scalar density placeholder, or an arbitrary pair of laws.

normalizations_and_actual_objects.obligation: H(lambda) is the signed full-Haar expectation of det(O) times the integral of h_lambda against the actual Gaussian density p_O; h_lambda(x)=exp(-lambda ||x||^2).
normalizations_and_actual_objects.consequence: A closed scalar RHS of Eq. 24 can replace H only through the canonical equality. Defining a new scalar gap equal to that RHS does not identify it with the actual measures' test gap.

normalizations_and_actual_objects.obligation: The spherical law used in the Poisson identities is probability-normalized and U = O_11 is the first coordinate of Oe_1 under full Haar.
normalizations_and_actual_objects.consequence: No unnormalized sphere-area factor may enter Eqs. 21-24.
